subject: Validity of the results from bup() when fitting models under maximum likelihood.

messages.author: 98b567f75758dc3a
messages.subject: Validity of the results from bup() when fitting models under maximum likelihood.
parts:
Hi all

I have been looking for a means of generating site-specific projected occupancy and the site-specific estimated latent occupancy state for my data. I aim to use the matrix of projected occupancy and the matrix of 0s and 1s to produce an ROC curve. 

I have looked in this google group for a way to extract this information and refer to the following thread (https://groups.google.com/g/unmarked/c/EXswfc9aG0U/m/MVdxWXtvAAAJ) 

I just wanted to confirm the validity of using the following code when my dynamic occupancy model has been fitted with the colext function rather than in a Bayesian framework.

  #Yearly Predicted Occupancy
> Site_specific_projected_occupancy = t(projected(Mallard,mean="F")[2,,])
> dim(Site_specific_projected_occupancy) #Dimension are sites and years

  #An estimate of true occupancy
> posterior_distribution_of_the_latent_occupancy_state  = bup(ranef(Mallard),
+                                                                                                               stat = 'mode')
> dim(posterior_distribution_of_the_latent_occupancy_state) #Dimension are sites and years

> Mean.AUC=c()
> for (i in 1:ncol(posterior_distribution_of_the_latent_occupancy_state)) {
+                 Mean.AUC[i] = auc(posterior_distribution_of_the_latent_occupancy_state[,i],
+                 Site_specific_projected_occupancy[,i])
+ }

# Plot of ROC
> plot.roc(posterior_distribution_of_the_latent_occupancy_state[,1],
+         Site_specific_projected_occupancy[,1],
+         percent=T,
+         col=brewer.pal(12,"Set3")[1])
Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
Setting direction: controls < cases
> for (i in 3:11) {
+  lines.roc(posterior_distribution_of_the_latent_occupancy_state[,i-1],
+            Site_specific_projected_occupancy[,i-1],
+            percent=T,
+            col=brewer.pal(12,"Set3")[i])
+ }

James
